revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched and are genuine and relevant (MISA on the Data Protection Act 18 of 2024, and the US trade.gov digital economy guide), but neither directly addresses data-exchange-specific transparency, so the score rested on thin support. Fresh search found that the Digital Services Bill referenced in the original comments has since been passed by Parliament (15 August 2025) and gazetted as the Digital Services Act, No. 22 of 2025 (BOCRA). Part V of this Act (ss.24-31) legally mandates an Enterprise Data Inventory, an annual public disclosure of data-asset usage, and a public open-data platform administered by the Authority - a forward-looking annual-reporting obligation, not yet evidenced in practice. The Global Digital Identity Index confirms Botswana already operates a general Open Data portal (botswana.opendataforafrica.org, updated annually, 'basic info/datasets' maturity) and a Government Service Bus for inter-agency data exchange, but also confirms there is no Right-to-Information law and no dedicated public dashboard specific to data-exchange governance or data-sharing agreements. On balance the evidence still supports 'Low - Limited Disclosure' (code 2): a legal annual-reporting requirement now exists but is very new (Aug 2025) with no demonstrated implementation yet, and no confirmed public dashboard or agreement-level disclosure for the data exchange system itself. Score confirmed unchanged; label cosmetic difference noted in the redteam flag is correct and non-substantive.
revised_comments: Botswana's transparency around government data-exchange operations remains limited. The Data Protection Act 18 of 2024 (in force from 14 January 2025) requires breach notification and record-keeping, overseen by the Information and Data Protection Commission, but does not itself mandate public disclosure of data-sharing agreements. The newly passed Digital Services Act, No. 22 of 2025 (enacted 15 August 2025) introduces a stronger legal framework, requiring public bodies to maintain an Enterprise Data Inventory and publish information on data-asset usage at least annually via a national open-data platform administered by the Botswana Communications Regulatory Authority. In practice, Botswana already runs a general Open Data portal (botswana.opendataforafrica.org), updated annually with basic datasets, and a Government Service Bus connecting agency systems, but there is no dedicated public dashboard or published register of data-sharing agreements specific to the data exchange system, and no Right-to-Information law compelling proactive disclosure. Overall disclosure is best characterised as low, with statutory annual-reporting obligations only recently introduced and not yet demonstrated in practice.
